stage1.impression: This is a striking idea: you look through a tunnel of oak doors to a lit room with a figure, two red-glowing speakers and a ringed orb. But it reads as a CG architectural visualization, not a night photograph. The near oak surfaces are large, smooth and evenly veneered, and the lit band across the top is the brightest and largest thing in the frame, so it pulls the eye away from the room. The hero sits in about 15 % of the frame, the figure is a featureless mannequin, and the orb's neon-rainbow rings read as signage or a nightclub. A design magazine would see a specific architectural move (the porch as a sound lock), but at this framing and exposure it would not run. It reads as a well-modelled proposal render, not a place.

blocking_9: The listening room (the Tropos pair and Mother EARF) must fill at least a third of the frame width; at present the porch jambs and lintel take about 75 % of the frame.
The lit band above the opening must stop being the brightest large area: its region [115,50,780,250] has lum_median 193 and must come down to about 110-130.
The frame's lum_median must fall from 61 to the 22-50 night range while the speaker regions keep a lum_median of 45 or more.

Near oak surfaces at 1:1 need real oiled-oak texture: open grain, end-grain and edge wear, slight unevenness, joints between boards. The left leaf at present reads as one smooth printed veneer and the right slotted face as perfectly uniform extrusions.
The figures need to read as people (clothing, hair, a glass in hand), not as grey clay mannequins.
There should be some sign of life in the foreground (the bar edge, a glass, a coat, a record) so the viewer is placed at the bar.

defects.what: The lit band or lintel panel is overexposed and flat (lum_median 193, p95 225). It reads as a lightbox, the vertical fin streaks look like soft banding, and it has no depth.
The near left oak leaf is bright (lum_median 111) with a large, uniform, CG-smooth veneer pattern and no edge wear. It steals attention from the room.
The slotted oak baffle is a perfectly regular set of identical boards with no grain variation. It reads as an extrusion or texture, not as oak.
The seated figure is a featureless grey mannequin (smooth head, no hair or clothing detail) and reads as a placeholder model.
Mother EARF's coloured rings (blue, green, yellow, pink) read as neon signage and add saturated colours beyond the speaker tint.
The left Tropos's red emissive frame is partly clipped (clip_pct 2.96) and reads as a glowing red box rather than tinted cast acrylic.
The right Tropos's red frame is clipped too (clip_pct 3.55) and has the same lightbox look.
The ceiling strip above the band is bright orange (r_median 208) and flat, a second hot band at the frame edge.
The right edge is an empty near-black strip (lum_median 13.6) with no detail. It reads as the end of the model.
The listening-room floor is a flat, featureless grey-brown with no end-grain or rug texture and no light pooling under the chairs.

changes.problem: The hero room is small and boxed in by about 75 % frame of door jambs and lintel, so the frame does not make you want to walk in.

evidence.measured: The listening room spans about 270 of 1200 px wide (22 %). The jambs [0,140,360,800] and [760,40,1140,800] plus the lintel [115,50,780,250] fill the rest.

change.to: 40 mm, camera moved about 1.5 m toward the porch (x about 11.1), same height and target

changes.expected: The opening and both Tropos fill about 40-50 % of the frame width, the porch still frames them on both sides, and the lit band is cropped to a thin strip at the top.

changes.problem: The band panel over the porch is blown toward white and is the dominant light in the frame.

evidence.measured: lum_median 193.3, p95 225, r/g/b medians 232/185/159 (a desaturated cream, not amber)

change.setting: the lantern's band emission / the baffle's graze

changes.expected: The band glows a warm amber at mid-tone, with the fins legible as separate edges, and no longer outshines the room.

changes.problem: The frame is too bright overall for a night interior.
changes.expected: The frame median falls to about 42-48, with deep but readable shadows on the jambs.

changes.problem: Once the exposure drops, the speakers would sink below legibility, and the room should be the brightest pool.

evidence.measured: lum_median 49.4 now (left speaker 41.3); a 0.4-stop exposure drop would take both to about 33-37

change.setting: inside the lantern: the pair spots / Mother EARF spot
change.to: 2 x 110 W, 28 deg; Mother 60 W, 22 deg

changes.expected: The Tropos and Mother EARF become the brightest pool in the frame, with faces readable and falloff into the slatted back wall.

changes.problem: The near left oak leaf is lit as brightly as the hero room and pulls the eye to the frame edge.

evidence.measured: lum_median 110.6, p95 192.8, brighter than the speakers (41-49)

change.setting: the route area / counter spots spill onto the porch leaf
change.from: route 0.1 W/m2; counter spots 4 x 38 W, 18 deg
change.to: route 0.04 W/m2; aim the nearest counter spot down onto the bar top (or flag it) so the leaf takes only spill

changes.expected: The near leaf falls to a dark warm oak with its edge catching light, framing the room rather than competing with it.

changes.problem: The oak reads as smooth CG veneer and uniform extrusions, not oiled oak.

evidence.measured: At 3x crop the boards are identical in tone and width, with no grain, end checks or unevenness. The left leaf shows one continuous, oversized flowing grain.

change.setting: the oak's finish within its kind
change.from: one uniform veneer texture, smooth spec
change.to: per-board random grain offset and ±8 % tone variation, real-scale rift or quarter-sawn grain (rays visible), roughness 0.45-0.6 with an oiled sheen, slight edge rounding and darkening at the board edges

changes.expected: At 1:1 the boards read as individual oiled oak pieces and the surfaces stop looking printed.

changes.problem: The people are grey clay mannequins and break the photograph instantly.

evidence.measured: A smooth uniform head and body with no hair, fabric or skin variation; shutter 0.8 is not enough to blur it into a person.

change.to: 2 clothed scanned figures (dark knit, hair, a glass in hand), shutter 1.5 with a small head turn so the motion blur hides the face

changes.expected: The seated listener reads as a real person in soft motion, which adds life without detail to scrutinise.

changes.problem: The foreground has no sign of life or place, so the viewer is not at a bar.

evidence.measured: Only bare oak jambs and a dark floor; the bar top and props are not in frame.

change.to: drop the camera about 10 cm so the quartzite bar edge enters the bottom 8 % of the frame, out of focus, with a half-full glass and a record sleeve on it

changes.expected: A soft, warm foreground layer places the viewer on a bar stool looking in, which adds depth and coziness.

out_of_scope.request: Replace or tone down Mother EARF's multicolour rings so the only saturated colour is the Tropos Ember tint
out_of_scope.why: Mother EARF is a fixed EARF product as placed. Her colours read as neon signage and cost points on 'one colour', but changing them is a product decision for the owner.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Tropos red acrylic frames read as tinted cast acrylic rather than emissive red boxes (thickness, polished glowing edges)
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's material and parts are off limits. Only its lighting (c4) can be changed here; if the red glow is the material itself, the owner has to revisit it.

out_of_scope.request: Reduce the size of the lintel band panel relative to the opening
out_of_scope.why: The band's place and fins are fixed architecture; only its light (c2) and the camera crop (c1) may change.
